M1.title: APPROVE A $150,000 PILOT AGAINST MATERIAL SHARED EXPOSURE
M1.body:
## Decision

Approve a four-week pilot ceiling of **$150,000** to:

- Verify continuity at Meridian and the East Delta manufacturing cluster.
- Obtain the specifications needed to assess independent routes.
- Run comparable supplier RFIs.
- Demonstrate the complete decision workflow in a working dashboard.

## Why action is justified

- IonPeak’s qualified dies constrain both power assemblers.
- Jade’s qualified substrates constrain C10 and B10 board routes.
- C10 has one disclosed manufacturer serving all products.
- C20 has one disclosed manufacturer serving P1 and P2.
- Meridian’s financial and delivery deterioration intersects the C20 path.
- Four confirmed manufacturers operate in Z01.

One week of P1/P2 represents approximately:

\[
\$1{,}144m \div 52 = \$22m
\]

of associated gross revenue-equivalent.

At an illustrative 25% contribution margin and zero usable coverage:

\[
\$22m \times 25\% = \$5.5m
\]

That is approximately **37 times the $150,000 pilot ceiling**. This is a stress comparison, not a loss forecast or claimed return on investment.

| Management question | Answer | Immediate decision |
|---|---|---|
| Where? | Z01 contains four manufacturers. IonPeak and Jade are the two documented qualified-input locks. Meridian reaches C20 in P1/P2. | Verify site operation, inventory, recovery and independent paths. |
| How confident? | Direct awards and qualifications are generally grade A. Upstream relationships and indicators are A/B. Capacity, inventory and recovery remain grade C. | Separate documented dependencies from verified interruption. |
| What next? | Open two U2 reviews, one U3 booking check and comparable RFIs for the priority routes. | Owner within 24h; evidence within 72h; decision by Day 14. |

| Initial focus | P3 screen | Business association | Required action |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Jade | **79.0** | All products | Independent substrate route and SITE-081 continuity. |
| IonPeak | **78.2** | All products | Independent die route and SITE-074 continuity. |
| Cobalt | **76.9** | Sole disclosed C10 manufacturer; all products | Board continuity and complete alternate C10 route. |
| Meridian | **76.7** | C20 → P1/P2; $1,144m annual association | First financial, film and coverage review. |
| Lumen | **70.7** | Shared input behind both power assemblers | Core specification and second-source evidence. |
| Orion | **70.5** | Shared input behind both power assemblers | Metallised ceramic specification and route review. |
| Umber | **69.8–85.5** | SiC wafers behind IonPeak | Finance, capacity, wafer and recovery evidence. |

## Pilot cost

| Item | Basis | Amount |
|---|---|---:|
| Internal specialist effort | 120 person-days × assumed $750 | $90,000 |
| Samples and supplier technical support | Planning allowance | $30,000 |
| Dashboard prototype and tools | Planning allowance | $10,000 |
| Contingency | Planning allowance | $20,000 |
| **Pilot ceiling** | Finance to validate | **$150,000** |

Full qualification, tooling, inventory, capacity reservation and production introduction require separate approval.

M3.title: USE AN ALLOCATION-AWARE, REPRODUCIBLE SCREENING INDEX
M3.body:
## Condition

\[
C = 0.35F + 0.35O + 0.30G
\]

## Priority screen

\[
P3 = 0.45C + 0.25B + 0.20S + 0.10E
\]

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **F** | Financial concern based on current ratio and net debt/EBITDA anchors. |
| **O** | Operating concern based on shipment timeliness and deterioration. |
| **G** | Geographic context based on physical hazard and logistics friction. |
| **B** | Unique associated product revenue ÷ $1,560m × 100. |
| **S** | Evidence-based switching constraint. |
| **E** | Maximum downstream Tier-1 planned allocation connected to the manufacturer through a confirmed component path. |

## Why the four priority terms are distinct

- **C** measures current supplier condition.
- **B** measures portfolio breadth.
- **S** measures whether an approved independent switch exists.
- **E** measures how much downstream award allocation intersects the path.

E does **not** estimate the upstream supplier’s purchasing share, order volume or spend.

## Management bands

- **≥70:** continuity and qualification workstream.
- **55–<70:** managed assessment.
- **<55:** monitoring, subject to the mandatory action floor.

## Mandatory action floor

Any node linked to either of the following remains in a managed workstream:

- A direct 100%-allocated Tier-1 component route.
- An explicit shared qualified input with no approved independent alternative.

This keeps ForgeLine, Grove and HarborSense active even when their numerical screen is below 55.

## Why Delta still requires action

Delta’s condition score is only **24.0**, but:

- It holds 100% of the disclosed C20 award.
- No approved replacement route is evidenced.
- Meridian supplies film into that route.
- Meridian has the relevant financial and delivery event.
- C20 reaches P1 and P2.

Delta’s **59.1** is therefore a managed assessment. Meridian receives the first review because its condition is **74.1** and EV-003 directly concerns it.

## Confidence

- **A:** scoped award, qualification record or specific technical confirmation.
- **B:** explicit scoped disclosure or complete indicators with definition limitations.
- **C:** missing decision-changing evidence.

Confidence does not alter the risk number. Event urgency also remains separate.

M5.title: MATCH EVENTS THROUGH IDENTIFIERS, ROLES, DATES AND PATHS
M5.body:
## Matching precedence

1. Exact internal entity or facility ID.
2. Verified registry number.
3. Exact legal name corroborated by role and site.
4. Curated alias with human review.
5. Curated geography-to-zone mapping.

A lower-precedence name resemblance cannot override a conflicting registry number, role or facility.

## Conflict veto examples

- REG-NO-4128 resolves to Ion Peak Trading. The phrase “Ion Peak” cannot then match IonPeak Semiconductor.
- Delta Consumer Plastics cannot match Delta Capacitor.
- Jade Holdings headquarters cannot replace Jade’s production site.
- An administrative move cannot become a production shutdown.
- A 2025 publication date cannot make a 2023-effective event current.

## Match confidence

| Grade | Meaning |
|---|---|
| High | Exact verified entity/site/registry match with no conflict. |
| Medium | Curated geographic crosswalk or corroborated legal name and role. |
| Low | Alias or incomplete geographic match pending confirmation. |
| Rejected | Higher-precedence identity, role or date conflict. |

## Urgency

| Grade | Definition | Response |
|---|---|---|
| **U1** | Verified material interruption or a dated usable-coverage gap. | Immediate containment and escalation. |
| **U2** | Credible watch or financial/operational constraint on a material confirmed path. | 24h owner, 72h evidence, Day-14 decision. |
| **U3** | Potential shipment effect without a demonstrated coverage gap. | Booking-level verification within 72h. |
| **U0** | Duplicate, stale, administrative or excluded. | Preserve audit trail; no production alert. |

Queue order: urgency → estimated time to coverage gap → P3 → product breadth.

M6.title: A SWITCH IS USEFUL ONLY IF CAPACITY AND INPUTS SURVIVE
M6.body:
| Existing switch | Planned share change | Required output multiple | Remaining constraint |
|---|---|---:|---|
| M10 → Aster | 60% → 100% | 1.67× | Same IonPeak dies; capacity unverified. |
| M10 → Boreal | 40% → 100% | 2.50× | Same IonPeak dies; capacity unverified. |
| M20 → Aster | 70% → 100% | 1.43× | Same dies, cores and ceramics. |
| M20 → Boreal | 30% → 100% | 3.33× | Same dies, cores and ceramics. |
| B10 → Grove | 80% → 100% | 1.25× | Same Jade substrate. |
| B10 → HarborSense | 20% → 100% | 5.00× | Same Jade substrate; MCU source unknown. |

These are share calculations, not evidence of available ramp capacity.

| Failure mechanism | Route to investigate | Approval question |
|---|---|---|
| Meridian film supply | Compatible base/metallised film and complete C20 replacement. | Can the resulting capacitor pass electrical, thermal, life and production tests? |
| IonPeak dies | Alternate compatible bare die or independent complete M10/M20. | Does the route remove SITE-074 and meet assembly requirements? |
| Jade substrates | Independent fabricated substrate or complete C10/B10. | Does the route remove SITE-081 and meet board, firmware and testing requirements? |
| Umber wafers | Compatible wafer through an operating receiving fab or independently produced die. | Can the receiving process accept it? |
| Kestrel MCU | Qualified MCU redesign. | Can architecture, firmware, peripherals, safety and lifecycle pass? |
| Lumen/Orion | Alternate core and ceramic paths or alternate assembly architecture. | Does the new route remove the specific shared input? |

**Key operating principle:** A replacement wafer cannot restore a closed receiving fab.

\[
\text{Coverage gap}=\max(0,\text{validated recovery time}-\text{usable coverage})
\]

Usable coverage must include approved accessible inventory, acceptable work in process, confirmed shipments and actual demand without double counting.

## Tie rule

For candidates in the same supply form:

1. Independence from incumbent ownership, sites and shared inputs.
2. Evidence for an eligible supplying factory.
3. Supplier risk, reviewed symmetrically for all tied candidates.
4. Committed capacity and qualification plan.

Where the first two are unknown, label **“parallel RFI; no sequence.”**

Initial independence, site and credit responses are due **14 October 2026**.

M8.title: FIT SCORING IS EXPLAINABLE AND DOES NOT OVERRIDE APPROVAL GATES
M8.body:
\[
\text{Fit}=35(T/5)+25(Ap/5)+15(Fp/5)+15(Sc/5)+10(Q/5)
\]

| Dimension | Weight | A score of 4 means |
|---|---:|---|
| Technical match | 35 | Specific relevant product or process. |
| Application relevance | 25 | Explicit target-use category. |
| Manufacturing footprint | 15 | Evidence of eligible independent supplying sites. |
| Commercial scale | 15 | Established production scale. |
| Qualification-enabling evidence | 10 | Applicable technical, quality or validation support. |

M9.title: COVER ALL SEVEN COMPONENTS AND COMMON INPUTS
M9.body:
| Component or input | Capability-screened route | Required validation |
|---|---|---|
| M10/M20 | Semikron Danfoss complete power-module/assembly route | Electrical and thermal interfaces; independent dies, cores and ceramics. |
| C10 | Jabil control-board manufacturing | Design authority, substrate source, MCU, firmware and testing. |
| C20 | TDK, Vishay and KEMET/Yageo complete DC-link capacitors | Voltage, ripple, ESR/ESL, life, package, site and capacity. |
| H10 | Protocase custom-machined enclosure; Maysteel custom fabrication | Actual drawing, tolerances, sealing, tooling and volume. |
| H20 | Wakefield Thermal cold plate; Mersen power-module thermal route | Complete H20 scope, coolant, flow, pressure, leakage and corrosion. |
| B10 | Eberspächer Vecture BMS electronics; Jabil board manufacturing | Standalone-board scope, design rights, MCU, substrate and testing. |
| Lumen cores | TDK, Ferroxcube and Magnetics | Core material, geometry, frequency, losses, temperature and available volume. |

## Corrections to weaker comparisons

- A standard Hammond enclosure does not establish equivalence to a custom machined H10.
- Inventus Power’s battery-pack capability does not establish a standalone B10 PCBA route.
- A data-centre liquid-cooling product does not establish a complete H20 route.
- Boyd Thermal was acquired by Eaton in 2026, so they cannot be counted as two independent suppliers. [www.eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/sg/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-completes-acquisition-of-leading-liquid-cooling-solutions-provider-boyd-thermal.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- TDK appearing in capacitors and cores creates a potential cross-component group concentration.
- KEMET and Ferroxcube group relationships must be checked before counting them as independent.
- Published ST–SiCrystal and Semikron Danfoss–Infineon relationships trigger programme-specific input checks. They do not prove that a proposed NovaDrive route uses those inputs.

A5.title: EXACT CALCULATION RULES
A5.body:
## Financial anchors

| Current ratio | Concern | Net debt/EBITDA | Concern |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| <0.75 | 100 | ≥6 | 100 |
| 0.75–<1 | 75 | 4–<6 | 75 |
| 1–<1.5 | 50 | 3–<4 | 50 |
| 1.5–<2 | 25 | 2–<3 | 25 |
| ≥2 | 0 | <2 | 0 |

\[
F = \text{average of available CR and ND/E concern anchors}
\]

For the five Tier-3 nodes where both are missing, calculate F as **0–100**.

## Operating calculation

\[
D=\operatorname{clip}(4(100-OT),0,100)
\]

\[
T=\operatorname{clip}(-5\Delta,0,100)
\]

\[
O=0.7D+0.3T
\]

\[
G=(Hazard+Logistics)/2
\]

## S anchors

| S | Evidence state |
|---:|---|
| 100 | Explicit shared qualified input without an approved independent source; or one disclosed qualified Tier-1 route at 100% allocation with no approved replacement evidenced. |
| 75 | One disclosed upstream source at the assessed node; independently approved alternative not evidenced, but sole-qualified status is not explicitly established. |
| 50 | Qualified independent alternative evidenced; capacity or recovery remains open. |
| 25 | Qualified independent alternative with committed usable capacity and feasible delivery. |
| 0 | Material dependency removed. |

## E rules

- For a direct Tier-1 manufacturer: highest disclosed planned allocation held by that manufacturer across affected components.
- For an upstream manufacturer: total Tier-1 planned allocation intersected by its confirmed input path within a component, capped at 100.
- E is a maximum downstream path-exposure measure.
- E is not upstream supplier share or actual purchased volume.

Direct values:

- Aster 70
- Boreal 40
- Cobalt 100
- Delta 100
- Estuary 100
- ForgeLine 100
- Grove 80
- HarborSense 20

Assessed upstream nodes receive E=100 because each confirmed path intersects either:

- all qualified Tier-1 power routes, or
- a 100%-allocated direct component route.

## Calculation controls

- Use unrounded inputs.
- Round only final displayed values.
- Use half-up rounding to one decimal.
- Do not convert missing data to zero.
- Do not sum overlapping product revenue.
- Do not interpret P3 as failure probability.
- Any increase in C, B, S or E cannot reduce P3.
- Any decline in current ratio or timeliness cannot improve the relevant concern score.
- Any increase in leverage, hazard or logistics friction cannot improve the relevant concern score.
- All component and priority weights must sum to 1.0.

A10.title: QUALIFICATION AND INDEPENDENCE GATES
A10.body:
| Gate | Evidence required |
|---|---|
| Technical | Signed specification comparison and accepted tests. |
| Factory | Named legal manufacturer, site and process. |
| Quality | Applicable current certificates, traceability and change control. |
| Capacity | Contracted output, yield, testing and ramp. |
| Independence | Ownership, sites, critical inputs and logistics mapped against incumbent. |
| Supplier risk | Current supplying-entity financial and continuity review. |
| Commercial | Price, tooling/IP, lead time and enforceable commitments. |
| Release | Engineering and Quality approval for the site/programme. |

## Independence rule

Compare complete paths from critical input to component to NovaDrive production.

A candidate does not remove the dependency where the proposed route retains the same:

- Parent ownership.
- Qualified die.
- Circuit substrate.
- Receiving fab.
- Constrained factory.
- Critical material.
- Logistics bottleneck.

A11.title: ASSUMPTIONS, REQUESTS AND ECONOMICS
A11.body:
## Assumptions register

| Assumption or limitation | Effect |
|---|---|
| Planned allocations are award shares. | They are not actual purchases or capacity. |
| B counts each product once. | Prevents overlapping revenue addition. |
| E measures downstream path coverage. | It is not upstream supplier volume. |
| Higher hazard/logistics index means more concern. | Used in G; definitions require confirmation. |
| Five Tier-3 financial records are missing. | Produces arithmetic intervals. |
| 52 equal weeks and equal product revenue per unit. | Used only in illustrations. |
| 25% contribution margin. | Scenario assumption requiring Finance validation. |
| Inventory, BOM quantities, spend, recovery and spare capacity are absent. | Required before quantified continuity or ROI conclusions. |
| Candidate research is dated 5 October 2026. | It cannot be projected back into the 2025 event snapshot. |

## Tier-3 requests

| Node | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Umber | Legal-entity finance, SiC specification, site output, usable coverage, customer concentration and recovery. |
| Warden | Copper-foil grade/site, Jade allocation, stock, finance, capacity and independent backup. |
| Xenon | Resin grade/site, Jade dependence, stock, finance and replacement validation. |
| Yarrow | Mineral specification/site, Orion allocation, coverage, finance and substitute approval. |
| Zenith | Polymer grade/site, Meridian allocation, creditor exposure, coverage, recovery and finance. |

Initial Umber and Zenith continuity evidence is due T0+72h. Full Tier-3 credit packs are due **14 October 2026**.

## Economic illustration

\[
\$1{,}144m \div 52=\$22m\text{ weekly gross revenue-equivalent}
\]

At an assumed 25% contribution margin:

\[
\$22m \times 25\%=\$5.5m\text{ contribution-equivalent per uncovered week}
\]

At an assumed eight-week validated recovery:

| Usable coverage | Uncovered period | Gross revenue-equivalent |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 weeks | 6 weeks | $132m |
| 4 weeks | 4 weeks | $88m |
| 8 weeks | 0 | $0 |

These scenarios are used to decide what evidence to collect. They are not expected losses.
